## Outage Report

### (1) First error burst — time & host

**`2026-01-18T03:17:42Z` on `api-07`** — the first line is:
```
ERROR api-07 db pool exhausted (max=20) waiting=14 path=/v1/orders
```
Within ~90 seconds the error cascaded across all API hosts (`api-01` through `api-08`), producing **301** db-pool-exhaustion errors between `03:17:42Z` and `03:19:22Z`.

### (2) Root cause

The PostgreSQL connection pool (max=20) was fully consumed — all 20 connections held open for an extended period — so new frontend requests waiting on a connection timed out after 14+ seconds, returning 503. The burst of 301 errors over ~2 minutes is the symptom; the cause was connections never being released.

### (3) Responsible job / user

`batch-01`, job **`reconcile-ledger`** (user=`svc-batch`).

Timeline:
```
03:15:03Z  reconcile-ledger started, db_conns=20
03:15:04Z – 03:16:39Z  acquired connections 1/20 … 20/20 (one every 5s, no releases)
                          pool fully consumed
03:17:42Z  first downstream 503 from pool exhaustion
03:41:30Z  reconcile-ledger finished (rows=48210112), finally released_conns=20
```

The job held every connection in the shared pool for **~26 minutes** without returning any, starving all other services. A proper fix would be to either give batch jobs their own isolated connection pool or enforce a per-job connection limit well under the global max (e.g., ≤10 of 20).
